findings.evidence: AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality.lean:92 `(R : Type u) [Field R]` and :114 `exact ⟨(moduleFinite_iff_isFinite_hopfSpec R H.unop).mpr hG.1, inferInstance, ...⟩`; FiniteDual/CartierDuality.lean header: "the algebraic core of Cartier duality over a general affine base"; grep for `baseChangeBialgEquiv` outside the new file returns nothing.
findings.fix: Either do the step that actually unblocks the target (the finite-locally-free object-property correspondence generalising `finiteCommAffineGroupSchemeProperty_inverseImage` off `[Field R]`), or restate the path honestly — e.g. that base-change compatibility of the affine dual is what lets the construction glue over a non-affine base — and say which downstream declaration will consume `baseChangeBialgEquiv`.
findings.issue: The description claims this PR "supplies the affine base-change compatibility needed to extend the existing field-level Spec transport in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AffineGroupScheme/CartierDuality.lean to a general base". That is false: the only use of [Field R] there is at CartierDuality.lean:114, where `inferInstance` supplies `Module.Projective` for free over a field. Generalising the transport needs a scheme-side finite-locally-free/flat property matching `Module.Finite ∧ Module.Projective`, not a base-change square. Meanwhile the algebraic Cartier anti-equivalence over a general affine base already exists on main (FiniteDual/CartierDuality.lean), and nothing in-repo consumes the new equivalence, so the Layer 4 target itself is no closer.

summary: Single coherent topic in the Cartier-duality lane, but the description's stated path is wrong: base change of the finite dual is not what blocks extending the field-level Spec transport to a general base, and the Layer 4 target statement is not advanced by this satellite.
